$^{13}$ Low: the 1991–2023 long-run net rate throughout; High (tick): the 2018–2023 rate persists; Very High:
    the 1991–2023 census-interval trend continues; instead of the 2018–2023 rate fading to the long-run
    rate with a 10-year half-life.
$^{14}$ 5 / 15 years instead of 10.
$^{15}$ the soil carbon loss of the lowest (Raw) / highest (Organic) soil order on every new footprint
    instead of the area-weighted mean over the soil orders of the Auckland land zoned for urbanisation.
$^{16}$ the materials factor of the lowest / highest single case study of each typology instead of the pooled
    typology factor.
$^{17}$ every factor held at 2025 instead of A1–A3 on the item paths of Horup et al. (2025) and A4–A5 falling
    1% per year.
$^{18}$ the lowest / highest pooled materials factor when each case study is left out in turn, instead of the
    pooled factor (a spread, not a confidence interval).
$^{19}$ items made in New Zealand with electricity-intensive production held at 2025 instead of following
    their Horup et al. (2025) path.
$^{20}$ A4–A5 on each item's own Horup et al. (2025) path / held at 2025 instead of the generic 1% per year
    decline (Resch et al. 2021).
$^{21}$ soil carbon loss also on replacement floor area instead of none on rebuilt footprints.
$^{22}$ items mapped to a proxy material held at 2025 instead of following the proxy's path.

$^{1}$ household size continues linearly from 2023 at the 2018–2023 census-interval pace instead of the
    Stats NZ household-size path rebased on 2023.
$^{2}$ Stats NZ 2024-base stochastic projection, 5th / 95th percentile path instead of the median.
$^{3}$ Stats NZ Low / High household-size variant (smaller / larger households) instead of the Medium
    variant.
$^{4}$ from the shape-preserving (PCHIP) end slope at 2043 the slope tapers to zero over 5 years, instead of
    a zero slope imposed at 2043 and household size held constant after 2043.
$^{5}$ the last published interval (2038–2043) linear at its secant slope, the slope then tapering to zero
    over 5 years, instead of a zero slope imposed at 2043 and household size held constant after 2043.
$^{6}$ the 2026 overbuild (building above need in 2026–2027 and its continuation, fading at ρ = 0.43)
    replaces existing dwellings instead of adding to the stock: no surplus, so no absorption payback and
    no soil carbon loss on it.
$^{7}$ new-dwelling size held at its 2016–2025 mean per typology instead of the 2023–2025 mean.
$^{8}$ 0.93 / 0.96 of consented dwellings completed instead of 0.945.
$^{9}$ the mean of the 1986–2023 censuses on one definition instead of the 2023 census value (5.39%).
$^{10}$ the 2026 overbuild absorbed by 2030 / 2045 instead of 2035.
$^{11}$ consents lagged 15 / 19 months instead of 17.
$^{12}$ consents to December 2025 and the projected 2026 population instead of consents to July 2026 and the
    observed 2026 population growth.

note: Reference 19,761 kt. One at a time: not additive, not a joint interval. "No effect": every case within 0.01% of the Reference.
